The operation does not handle two-factor authentication since the schema does not define any TFA-related fields such as totp_secret or recovery_codes.

The registration process is designed with security in mind, ensuring the password is never stored in plain text and all operations comply with industry security standards for credential storage. The firstname, lastname, and phone fields are not included in the request body because the schema does not include these fields, even though they may be common in other systems. The password_reset_token and password_reset_expires fields are included to support password reset functionality, which is supported by the schema.

The operation is not subject to rate limiting or IP whitelisting constraints that might be enforced externally, as those mechanisms are not part of the database schema and are handled by separate infrastructure components. The admin account begins in an active state (is_active: true) unless the system has specific configuration requiring manual approval, which is not supported by this schema.

This registration process is the only way new admin accounts can be created within the system according to the defined schema, and it is only accessible to the service's provisioning mechanisms, not to end-users.

The login operation is the primary means of accessing administrative functionality, and its security is critical for system integrity. All session management occurs through the separate todo_app_admin_sessions table, ensuring separation of authentication state from user identity data. Create a new todo item for the authenticated user. This operation allows users to add individual tasks to their personal todo list. The system validates the todo title for length and content according to business rules defined in 03-business-rules.md, which require titles to be non-empty and under 255 characters.

The operation is restricted to authenticated users only. The user_id is automatically derived from the authentication token and mapped to the todo_app_todos table. Duplicate titles are prevented by the composite unique constraint on (user_id, title) in the database, ensuring users cannot create multiple identical todo items.

After successful creation, the system returns the full created todo item with its generated ID and timestamp, allowing the client to update its local representation immediately. Any validation errors are returned as 400 Bad Request with details about the specific field violation.

responseBody.description: The newly created todo item with all fields including generated ID, creation timestamp, and user association

The operation returns the updated entity state for client-side synchronization.

The update is permissioned to the authenticated user who owns the todo item, as determined by the user_id foreign key relationship with the todo_app_users table.

According to 03-business-rules.md, there is a 10-minute editability window after creation during which updates are permitted. Attempts to update a todo item after this window expires return a 403 Forbidden response. The system enforces title validation rules identical to those for creation (non-empty, under 255 characters).

The operation accepts partial updates — if only the title is provided, the description remains unchanged. If the todo item does not exist or does not belong to the authenticated user, a 404 Not Found response is returned.

The response body contains the full updated todo item, including the modified fields and the updated_at timestamp which is automatically set by the system.

operations.description:
This operation permanently removes a specific todo item from the system database. This is a hard delete operation that completely removes the record from the todo_app_todos table without any possibility of recovery.

The operation requires authentication and checks user ownership or administrative privileges before execution. A user can only delete their own todo items unless they have admin privileges. Admin users can delete any todo item in the system.

The todo item is identified by its unique todoId, which must match the id field in the todo_app_todos table. The operation does not accept a request body as the todo identifier is provided in the URL path.

After successful deletion, the system returns a 204 No Content response with no body. If the todo item does not exist, returns a 404 Not Found response. Attempts to delete without proper authorization return 403 Forbidden.

This operation does not trigger any audit log creation itself; audit logs for deletion are created automatically by the system as a side effect of the operation in the todo_app_audit_logs table.

The system automatically sets this field when an admin account is created. This timestamp is used for audit trails, accounting for account age, and understanding user growth patterns over time.

This field is not modifiable after creation and is included in API responses.

last_password_change.description:
Timestamp of the last time the admin password was changed. This corresponds to the "last_password_change" column in the todo_app_admins Prisma model.

This field helps implement password expiration policies and security audits. It is automatically updated every time the password is changed through the proper password change workflow.

Note: This field is not updated when a password is set during account creation, only when explicitly changed later.

recovery_email.description:
Secondary email address for account recovery purposes. This corresponds to the "recovery_email" column in the todo_app_admins Prisma model.

This address is used exclusively for password recovery and security notifications. It does not need to be the same as the primary email address and can be a personal or alternative work email.

This field is optional and can be configured by the admin user if password reset functionality is required.

timezone.description:
Timezone identifier for the admin account. This corresponds to the "timezone" column in the todo_app_admins Prisma model.

Uses IANA timezone database format (e.g., "America/New_York", "Asia/Tokyo", "Europe/London"). This setting determines how timestamps are displayed in the user interface and affects scheduled operations.

Defaults to "UTC" if not explicitly set during account creation.

password_reset_token.description:
Random token generated for password reset requests. This corresponds to the "password_reset_token" column in the todo_app_admins Prisma model.

This token is generated when a user initiates a password reset request and is sent to the primary email address. It is used to verify the user's intent to change their password.

The token expires after a set time period (typically 24 hours) as indicated by the password_reset_expires field.

password_reset_expires.description:
Expiration timestamp for the password reset token. This corresponds to the "password_reset_expires" column in the todo_app_admins Prisma model.

This timestamp determines when the password reset token becomes invalid. After this time, the user must request a new password reset token.

The system automatically sets this value when a password reset token is generated and will reject any reset attempts made after this time has passed.

last_login.description:
Timestamp of the admin's most recent successful login. This corresponds to the "last_login" column in the todo_app_admins Prisma model.

This field is updated to the current timestamp upon every successful authentication. It provides an audit trail of when the admin last accessed the system and can be used for security monitoring and account activity reporting.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether the admin account is currently active and able to authenticate. This corresponds to the "is_active" column in the todo_app_admins Prisma model.

An inactive account cannot be used for authentication, even with correct credentials. This provides a mechanism to disable accounts without permanently deleting them.

The default value is true. A false value indicates the account has been disabled by an administrative action.

ITodoAppAdmin.description:
Admin entity representing system administrators with elevated privileges.

This represents a complete administrative account in the TodoApp system capable of managing users, viewing audit logs, and configuring system settings.

This schema corresponds directly to the todo_app_admins Prisma model and includes all fields defined in that model. For security reasons, sensitive information like password_hash is excluded from API responses. You'll see this schema used in GET /todoApp/admin/admins/{adminId} when retrieving an admin account.

The schema includes all fields from the Prisma model:
- id (UUID)
- email (string)
- password_hash (hashed password)
- created_at (timestamp)
- last_password_change (timestamp)
- recovery_email (optional email for recovery)
- timezone (IANA timezone identifier)
- password_reset_token (reset token)
- password_reset_expires (token expiration)
- last_login (timestamp)
- is_active (boolean status)

All fields are required in the database except recovery_email and password_reset_token/expiration (which are NULLable until used).

Some fields are only used internally and never exposed to clients:
- password_hash: Stored in database but never returned in API responses
- password_reset_token & password_reset_expires: Used only during password reset flow

Other fields are exposed contextually:
- id: Always exposed in responses that reference admin accounts
- email: Exposed in profile information but not in authentication responses
- created_at, last_password_change, last_login, is_active: Exposed for audit and status purposes
- timezone, recovery_email: Exposed for user configuration

This ensures a comprehensive yet secure representation of admin accounts that aligns exactly with the database schema.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin account.

This field corresponds to the 'id' column in the todo_app_admins Prisma model.

This is the primary key for the admin account and is used to uniquely identify each administrator in the system.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

email.description:
Email address of the admin account.

This field corresponds to the 'email' column in the todo_app_admins Prisma model.

This is the primary authentication identifier for administrative accounts.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

role.description:
Admin role designation.

This field corresponds to the 'role' column in the todo_app_admins Prisma model.

Possible values include 'admin', 'super_admin', or other role types defined by the system.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

ITodoAppAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Response body for successful admin authentication that contains only the identifying information about the authenticated admin account. This is returned after successful login via POST /auth/admin/login or POST /auth/admin/join.

This authorized response is designed to provide a secure way to identify an authenticated admin without exposing sensitive information like password hashes or authentication tokens.

This is a minimal identity representation suitable for use in authorization contexts.

Fields:
- id: Unique identifier (UUID format)
- email: Primary email address
- role: Administrative role designation

Note: This schema intentionally excludes timestamps (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) and other metadata to minimize data exposure in authentication responses.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

email.description:
The admin's registered email address used for authentication.

This field maps directly to the "email" column in the todo_app_admins Prisma schema. It serves as the primary identifier for administrative users during login.

CRITICAL: This field is required for all login attempts. The system validates that the email exists in the user database before attempting password verification.

Examples: "admin@company.com", "system@todoapp.local"

Security Note: This field should never be used as a display name - it is purely an authentication credential.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

password.description:
The plaintext password provided by the admin user for authentication.

This field contains the user's password as submitted during login. The system performs server-side hashing with PBKDF2 and compares it against the stored password_hash in the todo_app_admins table.

CRITICAL: This field is required for authentication. Passwords must meet minimum security requirements:
- Minimum 8 characters
- Maximum 128 characters
- Should include a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters

The system never logs, stores, or transmits the plaintext password after authentication.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

ip.description:
The IP address from which the authentication request originated.

This field captures the client's network address for security auditing and session tracking purposes. It corresponds to data that would be collected from the HTTP request headers when an admin logs in.

CRITICAL: This field is required to populate the todo_app_admin_sessions table with connection metadata.

The format must be either a valid IPv4 address (e.g., "192.168.1.1") or a valid IPv6 address (e.g., "2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334").

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

href.description:
The full URL of the page from which the authentication request was initiated.

This field captures the source page context for security audit trails. It allows system administrators to track whether logins originated from expected locations (e.g., the official login page at https://todoapp.com/login).

CRITICAL: This field is required for comprehensive security logging. It cannot be reliably extracted from request headers as clients may omit the Referer header.

Examples: "https://todoapp.com/login", "https://todoapp.com/"

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

referrer.description:
The URI of the website or resource that linked to the authentication page.

This field captures external referral sources for traffic analysis and security monitoring. It complements the href field to distinguish between direct access and referral-based login attempts.

CRITICAL: This field is required to maintain complete audit trails of user navigation patterns leading to authentication.

Examples: "https://google.com/search?q=todoapp", "https://company.com/internal-tools"

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

ITodoAppAdmin.IAuth.description:
Request payload for authenticating an admin user with email and password. Contains only the credentials required for login. The system hashes the provided password and compares it against the stored password_hash in the todo_app_admins table. No other fields are present since the database schema does not define username, two-factor authentication codes, or other authentication factors. This is a direct representation of the minimal authentication requirements defined in the Prisma model.

This DTO is used in the POST /auth/admin/login endpoint which is a self-authentication operation where the admin is logging themselves in. The session context fields are required for this operation because:
- The admin account is being accessed by the end user (self-authentication)
- The system needs to record IP address, href, and referrer to populate todo_app_admin_sessions with connection metadata
- A new session record will be created upon successful authentication

The password field maps to the password_hash column in the todo_app_admins Prisma schema. The system receives plain text password, hashes it with PBKDF2, and stores it as password_hash in the database. This is the standard field name mapping pattern.

Session context fields are required because this is a direct authentication request from a user, not an administrative action.

Security Note: The password must be transmitted over HTTPS only. The system never stores, logs, or transmits the plain text password after authentication.

Examples of fields:
{
  "email": "admin@company.com",
  "password": "SecurePass123!",
  "ip": "192.168.1.1",
  "href": "https://todoapp.com/login",
  "referrer": "https://google.com/search?q=todoapp"
}

Important: The "ip" field is optional because the server will extract it from the HTTP request if not provided. The "href" and "referrer" are mandatory because they cannot be reliably extracted from the request context and are needed for audit trail integrity.

refreshToken.description:
The refresh token used to obtain a new access token without re-authentication.

This token is issued during initial login and stored in the todo_app_admin_sessions table. It allows for extended user sessions without requiring re-entry of credentials.

CRITICAL: This field is required for the token refresh operation. The token must be valid, not expired, and associated with an active admin account.

Refresh tokens typically have longer lifetimes (7-30 days) and are stored securely on the client side.

Examples: "rt_abcd1234efgh5678ijkl"

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

ITodoAppAdmin.IRefresh.description: Request payload for refreshing admin authentication tokens. Contains only the refresh token as the sole authentication mechanism. This token is provided by the system during the initial login and is used to obtain a new access token without requiring the user to re-enter credentials. The schema does not include fields for additional authentication factors or user identifiers since these are derived from the token's metadata.

email.description:
Updated email address for user account.

This field corresponds to the 'email' column in the todo_app_users Prisma model.

Users may update their email address to a new valid format. The system will validate uniqueness and format before applying changes.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

password_hash.description:
Updated password hash for user account.

This field corresponds to the 'password_hash' column in the todo_app_users Prisma model.

Users may update their password by providing a new bcrypt-hashed value. The client should never send plain text passwords directly.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

deleted_at.description:
Soft delete timestamp for user account.

This field corresponds to the 'deleted_at' column in the todo_app_users Prisma model.

Setting this timestamp will logically delete the user account, making it inactive while preserving data. Users cannot self-delete accounts through this field.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

ITodoAppUser.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing user account in the todoApp system. This schema defines the fields that can be modified by authenticated users. All properties are optional to allow partial updates. Ownership validation ensures that users can only modify their own accounts. This update request allows users to modify their account details including email and password via the PUT /todoApp/user/users/{userId} endpoint.

Fields:
- email: New email address (optional) - must be unique and valid format
- password_hash: New bcrypt-hashed password (optional) - client should hash password before sending
- deleted_at: Set to a timestamp to logically delete account (optional) - admin function only

Note: The client should never send plain text passwords. Password updates must be pre-hashed using bcrypt algorithm before submission.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

created_after.description:

deleted.description:

- true: Return only deleted accounts
- false: Return only active accounts
- null or omit: Return both deleted and active accounts

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

The schema does not include any fields from the todo_app_admins table directly (like email, created_at, etc.) but instead provides search parameters that filter based on those fields.

Note: All response fields are defined in IPageITodoAppAdmin.ISummary, while this schema only contains query parameters for extraction.

System-managed fields like updated_at and deleted_at are not queryable through this schema as they require administrative authorization that is not associated with user-driven search operations.

ITodoAppAdmin.IUpdate.description:

This schema contains all assignable properties for updating an admin entity. All fields are optional to support partial updates. Ownership fields like adminId and creation timestamps are immutable and cannot be modified through this interface.

Used exclusively in PUT /todoApp/admin/admins/{adminId} operations. Does not allow modification of authentication credentials or system-managed fields.

Note: This DTO deliberately excludes password, session, and security token fields - these are managed through separate secure endpoints.

id.description:
Primary Key. Unique identifier for the todo item, generated automatically upon creation using UUID v4 format.

This identifier is immutable and serves as the canonical reference for this specific task across all system components. The UUID format ensures global uniqueness without requiring centralized coordination, allowing distributed systems to create new todo items independently.

user_id.description:
The authenticated user who created this todo item. {@link todo_app_users.id}.

This foreign key permanently associates the todo item with the user who created it, ensuring data isolation and proper ownership. The value is automatically derived from the authentication token and cannot be modified by client requests.

title.description:
The text content of the todo item. Must be between 1 and 255 characters. Whitespace-only strings are not allowed. This is the only user-editable field besides completion status. Field must be non-null per business requirement.

This field represents the core description of the task and must be meaningful enough for users to identify the item's purpose. The business rules require titles to be non-empty and under 255 characters to ensure usability and database consistency. This field is user-provided and is the only required property in the request body during creation.

description.description:
An optional detailed description of the todo item. This field allows users to provide additional context, instructions, or notes about the task.

If provided, the description must be a string with no specified length limit, though practical considerations suggest keeping it reasonable for display purposes. If omitted, the system will store this field as null in the database.

The description is not indexed for search and is primarily intended for user reference. It follows the same privacy model as the todo item itself - accessible only to the owning user and administrators.

completed.description:
Binary flag indicating if the todo item has been completed. Default is false when created. Users may toggle this status any number of times. This represents state, not progress.

This field is a persistence layer representation of a task's completion state in the business domain. A value of true means the task has been fully completed according to the user's intent, while false indicates it remains in an active or pending state.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo item was created. Set automatically by system upon creation and immutable thereafter.

This field follows the ISO 8601 date-time format and is generated by the system at the time of creation. It cannot be modified by client requests and represents the true creation time in UTC timezone according to system clock.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo item was last updated (title or completion status changed). Updated automatically by system.

This field follows the ISO 8601 date-time format and is maintained by the system as a record of when the last meaningful change occurred to the todo item (either the title or completion status). This enables users to see recent updates and supports audit trails.

ITodoAppTodo.description:
Represents a single todo item in the system. This is the primary data structure returned when retrieving a todo item by its unique identifier.

The object contains all relevant information about the todo item, including its core properties (title, description), system-generated fields (id, timestamps), and ownership information (user_id).

This DTO follows the principles of the atomic operation principle by providing complete information within a single response, enabling clients to render the full todo item without requiring additional API calls. The structure ensures that the data consistently reflects the state of the corresponding todo_app_todos table in the database, with all fields mapping directly to their Prisma schema counterparts.

The data model satisfies 3NF as all fields depend solely on the primary key and there are no transitive dependencies. This ensures data integrity and prevents anomalies during updates.

All fields have explicit relationships to the Prisma schema: user_id references todo_app_users.id, title has a 1-255 character constraint, completed is a boolean with default false, and both created_at and updated_at follow the ISO 8601 date-time format.

search.description:
Minimal search query string to match against todo item titles.

This optional field allows users to search for todo items by partial text matching against the title field.

When provided, the system performs a case-insensitive substring search across all todo items belonging to the authenticated user. The search is performed server-side and can include spaces and special characters.

For example, a search term of 'email' would return todos with titles like 'Send email to John', 'Read email', and 'Email templates'.

If null or empty string is provided, the search will not be applied and all items will be returned.

completed.description:
Filter todo items by completion status.

This optional field allows users to filter the result set to show only completed items, only incomplete items, or all items.

When true, only todo items with completed: true are returned.
When false, only todo items with completed: false are returned.
When null, all todo items regardless of completion status are returned.

This provides a flexible filtering mechanism that can be combined with other search criteria.

created_after.description:
Filter todo items to only include those created after this timestamp.

This optional field allows users to retrieve todo items created after a specific date and time.

The value must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-12-01T10:30:00Z').

When provided, only todo items with created_at greater than the specified timestamp will be returned. This is useful for retrieving new items since a previous query or for time-bounded analysis.

created_before.description:
Filter todo items to only include those created before this timestamp.

This optional field allows users to retrieve todo items created before a specific date and time.

The value must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-12-01T10:30:00Z').

When provided, only todo items with created_at less than the specified timestamp will be returned. This is useful for retrieving old items or for time-bounded analysis.

page.description:
The page number for paginated results.

This required parameter specifies which page of results to return. Pagination starts at page 1.

Page numbers must be positive integers. The system enforces a minimum page of 1 to prevent invalid pagination requests. The default value is 1, which returns the first page of results when page parameter is not explicitly provided by the client.

limit.description:
The maximum number of todo items to return per page.

This required parameter specifies the page size for the paginated results.

Valid values range from 1 to 100 items per page, with a default of 20. This constraint prevents excessively large result sets that could impact server performance.

The maximum limit of 100 ensures that no single request will cause significant performance degradation or memory pressure on the server.

ITodoAppTodo.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching and filtering a paginated list of todo items.

This schema defines the structure of the request body for the PATCH /todoApp/user/todos endpoint, which performs filtered searches on the user's todo items.

It combines search criteria (search, completed, created_after, created_before) with pagination parameters (page, limit) and sorting options (sort_by, order) into a single cohesive request type.

All properties are explicitly documented to ensure clients can make proper use of this advanced filtering capability, which supports complex query combinations tailored to user needs.

This type enables users to efficiently find specific todo items among potentially large collections, with fine-grained control over results through combination of search, filter, sort, and pagination parameters.

All parameters support null values (except the required ones) to allow flexible combinations. For example, a client can search for title 'email' with completed: false without specifying created_after or created_before.

ITodoAppAuthLog.description:
Authentication logs record all login attempts, both successful and failed, by users and administrators. This table is critical for security monitoring and compliance. Each entry includes the actor type, IP address, and timestamp. Used to detect brute force attacks and unauthorized access attempts. Indexes on actor_type and created_at enable efficient query patterns for security analytics.

### Key Security Considerations:

- The `success` field tracks authentication outcomes for fraud detection
- The `actor_type` field identifies actor role (user/admin) but does not expose specific IDs
- The `created_at` field timestamps events for audit trail purposes
- No sensitive fields like ip, referrer, or system-managed timestamps are exposed in this response
- User and admin identifiers are kept private - authentication context comes from JWT token in HTTP headers, not response body

This response format follows zero-trust principles by exposing only necessary, non-sensitive information for logging compliance and security monitoring.\n\n\n### New change: actor_id field added to enable traceability
\n\nAlthough sensitive user/admin identifiers are normally protected, the actor_id field has been added with nullable: true to enable security investigations and compliance audits while maintaining privacy. When this field is populated, it allows correlation of authentication events to specific user/admin accounts. This field is excluded from public-facing audit log views (like ITodoAppAuthLog.ISummary) where it is not needed, but is available for internal security teams with appropriate permissions.\n\nThis approach balances security with traceability requirements.

This field records the full user agent header from the HTTP request that triggered the audit event.

It identifies the browser, operating system, and device type that generated the request.

This information can be used to detect unusual access patterns or potential security threats.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

createdAt.description:
The timestamp when the audit log entry was created.

This field records when the system generated the audit record, not when the original action occurred (which can be inferred from the request timestamp).

It should be automatically set by the system using UTC time.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

ITodoAppAuditLog.description:
Audit logs track all administrative actions performed on the system, including user account management, todo item access/modification/deletion, and system configuration changes. This table ensures accountability and supports regulatory compliance. Each entry records who performed the action, what was modified, and when. Reference: {@link todo_app_admins.id} for the admin actor, {@link todo_app_users.id} for affected users, and {@link todo_app_todos.id} for modified todo items.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

The token contains claims about the user (e.g., user ID, roles) signed by the server.

It has a short expiration time (typically 15-60 minutes) to minimize security risk.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires, extending the user's session.

It has a longer expiration time (typically 7-30 days) and is stored securely on the client.

Security Note: The refresh token should be transmitted over HTTPS and stored securely (e.g., in HTTP-only cookies).

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and can no longer be used for authentication.

This information is used by the server to determine token validity.

The client should not use this field for expiration decisions - it should trust the JWT signature and expiration claim.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

This information is used by the server to determine when the refresh token is no longer valid.

The client should not use this field for refresh decisions - it should trust the refresh token's signature and expiration claim.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.

ITodoAppAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend applications.

CRITICAL SECURITY RULE: This type is used internally by the authentication service and MUST NOT be exposed in any API response body. Only the HTTP Authorization header should contain tokens.

> MUST be written in English. Never use other languages.
